provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Out family batch. Problem-driven and urgent: buyers arrive after a storm with water where it shouldn't be, so the kit leans on diagnosis, engineering and repair. No wall block or drain product brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Where is the water going? Yard drainage diagnosis
pageStructurePlus.contains: Soggy lawn, standing water after storms, water against the foundation, a wet basement wall, washed-out mulch beds, and a symptom checker that points to the likely fix
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners know the symptom, not the solution. A diagnosis page turns a vague worry into a booked site visit.

pageStructurePlus.section: French drains, dry wells and downspout lines
pageStructurePlus.contains: How a French drain works, channel drains at the driveway, buried downspout lines, pop-up emitters, dry wells and swales, and which fixes which problem
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers have heard the word French drain and little else. Explaining the options shows you sell the right fix, not the biggest one.

pageStructurePlus.contains: When a wall over 4 feet needs an engineer, geogrid, drainage stone and pipe behind the wall, surcharge from driveways, and who handles the permit
pageStructurePlus.why: Walls fail from water behind them, not from the face. Buyers who see the engineering trust the price.

pageStructurePlus.section: Leaning, bulging and failing wall repair
pageStructurePlus.contains: Rotting timber walls, bulging block walls, cracked poured walls, tie-backs, partial rebuilds, and when the whole wall has to come out
pageStructurePlus.why: A leaning wall is an urgent, worried call. A repair page catches it before the owner panics and calls whoever answers.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Terracing a hillside, regrading so water runs away from the house, swales between neighbours, rock armour on steep banks, and planting to hold soil
pageStructurePlus.why: Hillside lots and neighbour runoff are common triggers. Showing the full menu of erosion control earns the bigger site visit.

designDirections.name: Engineered Slope

openers.line: Someone in {City} with water pooling against the foundation searches for yard drainage and finds {Business Name} with no site. They need to see you've fixed one like theirs before they call.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What that worried homeowner would find instead: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing sends people to Facebook, where a finished boulder wall is buried under weeks of posts. A homeowner with a leaning wall wants a repair page and a way to send pictures, fast.
openers.hook: Tap the link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest wall or drain job there.
openers.linkLine: A wall and drainage site instead of a feed: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing has a free-host banner and only talks about landscaping. Nothing on it says French drains or retaining walls, which is exactly what people search after a storm.
openers.hook: Open their site and check whether drainage or walls even appear. Note what's missing.
openers.linkLine: Your wall and drainage work, named the way people search: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site's contact page doesn't load on a phone. People look up drainage help standing in a flooded yard, phone in hand, right after the rain stops.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your drainage site, working on a phone in the rain: {demo-link}

openers.angle: No way to send the problem
openers.line: There's no way to show {Business Name} the problem without a phone call. A form that takes a few pictures of the wet spot or the leaning wall would let you triage before driving out.
openers.hook: Check listing, bios and any site for a form with picture upload. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A request form that takes pictures of the wall or the water: {demo-link}

openers.line: The tiered block wall and the boulder terrace on your Instagram are the kind of work that sells itself. They're mixed in with equipment posts where a buyer won't find them.
openers.hook: Find two finished walls or drain jobs you can name. Use one by name if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your walls and drainage jobs, sorted by problem solved: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews talk about a yard that finally drains and a basement that stayed dry through the last storm. That's what the next worried homeowner needs to read, and it never leaves your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about water, a wall or a dry basement. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the drainage fixes they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: After a storm like last week's, half of {City} is looking at water where it shouldn't be. The drainage contractor they find that night is the one who gets the work.
openers.hook: Use within a week of heavy rain, snowmelt or a named storm in their area. Name the storm in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready for the calls after the next storm: {demo-link}

openers.line: Water comes into basements at two in the morning, not during business hours. A drainage request form that takes pictures catches that homeowner while they're still mopping.
openers.hook: Call the listed number after hours. A generic or full voicemail means the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A drainage request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring an operator for your wall crew. People who can run an excavator and set block well look at your finished walls before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the role and date.
openers.linkLine: A retaining wall company site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You build walls in the hillier towns around {City}, but nothing tells a homeowner in {Neighborhood} you work there. 'Retaining wall' plus their town is the search.
openers.hook: Find the towns in their captions or reviews; pick the hilliest one they name.
openers.linkLine: A wall and drainage page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you finance retaining walls, say so on the repair page. A failing wall is a bill nobody planned for, and payments are often the first question.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing anywhere public. If not, skip.
openers.linkLine: Wall repair financing explained up front: {demo-link}

openers.line: Taller walls usually need an engineer and a permit, and homeowners know a failed wall is expensive. Showing your licence, insurance and the engineers you work with settles the first worry.
openers.hook: Check the state contractor registry for a record. Never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and engineering on one wall page: {demo-link}

openers.line: I'd guess plenty of your drainage work comes from waterproofers and home inspectors who point to the yard. Those referrals still look you up first.
openers.hook: Look for reviews mentioning an inspector, waterproofer or neighbour. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a drainage referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is solid wall work, straight courses and proper drainage stone behind it. A stranger should see that first, not three scrolls down.
openers.hook: Pick their newest finished wall or drain job and name it: material, height, problem solved, the town if tagged.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} is a well-built wall, and you can see the drainage stone behind it.

I searched for retaining wall and drainage contractors in {City} and found {Business Name} on Maps, but no site where a homeowner can describe the water problem and send pictures. I built a sample site to show how that could work, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my note got buried. Here's the sample wall and drainage site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a symptom checker for wet yards, a request form that takes pictures of the problem, and a page on French drains and wall engineering. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave it.
sequence.call:
"Hi, {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}. I build websites for drainage and retaining wall contractors in {City}. I sent you a message about a sample site. Did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No worries. It's a sample site for {Business Name} with a drainage symptom checker, a form that takes pictures of the wet spot or the leaning wall, and your walls sorted by problem solved, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk
"It's {Build Range} depending on how many problem and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For your outfit I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is less than the drainage stone on one wall."
"Can we go through it for ten minutes, Tuesday or Thursday?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice, and it's live before the next big rain."

objections.objection: My phone already rings off the hook after storms.
objections.handler: "That's when you need it most. The picture form lets you sort the real wall failures from the puddles before you drive anywhere."

objections.objection: Most of my work comes from landscapers and inspectors.
objections.handler: "Those referrals are gold. The homeowner still searches your name before calling, and a drainage page with finished jobs is what convinces them."
"You don't need to be. You text me pictures of finished walls and drains, and I handle the rest. Changes are a text too."

objections.objection: People think drainage should be cheap.
objections.handler: "Until they see what a failed wall costs. The site shows the pipe, stone and fabric behind your work, and that's what makes your number make sense."
"Those drainage leads go to several contractors at once. Your own site sends the person with the soggy yard to you alone."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: a symptom checker, a picture request form, a wall engineering page and a few town pages. Less than one dry well."

email.subject: Drainage and wall site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for drainage and wall contractors in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll text the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, the {Business Name} drainage demo comes down Friday so I can clear space.

Want it left up? Just say yes or no.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner}, the wet season's coming and the soggy-yard calls come with it. Thought of {Business Name}.

The sample site is still up, same price: {demo-link}

bullets: Price by problem solved, not by page: wet yard, wet basement wall, failing wall and eroding slope each get a page and a price line.
The picture request form is the core of a drainage site. It saves a drive per bad lead, so price it as its own line.
Peg the build to the drainage stone and pipe on one mid-size job, never to hours.
Include the engineering and permit page only for contractors who build walls tall enough to need one.
Charge for a storm-response banner and page; it pays for itself the first rainy week.
Keep town pages focused on hillier and wetter towns, where the searches actually come from.

lineItems.item: Problem page (wet yard, wall failure, erosion; each)
lineItems.description: Max with a before-and-after set, a short explainer diagram and a matching FAQ.

lineItems.item: Picture request form with problem triage
lineItems.description: Max with multi-picture upload, a symptom checklist and routing for urgent wall failures.
Max when it covers several towns' wall height rules and shows the engineers the client works with.
Max with an urgent request path, a what-to-document checklist and a switch the client can flip after storms.
Max when each town page gets finished local jobs and soil or slope notes.
Max for a full set of custom diagrams: French drain, dry well, wall section and swale.

whatElseYouSell.name: Rain-day drainage video shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Film a finished drain working in the rain, water going into the grate and out at the pop-up. Nothing proves drainage work like that clip."
whatElseYouSell.when: The next forecast rain after a finished drainage job.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts of walls and drains
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each finished wall or drain goes on your Maps profile with the problem it fixed and the town, so storm searchers see you first."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after the first storm
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After the first real rain on a finished drainage job, the homeowner gets a text asking how it held up and for a review."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, timed to the next storm.

whatElseYouSell.name: Storm-week drainage ad push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A ready-to-go campaign for French drains and wall repair switches on in the days after heavy rain, aimed at the wettest neighbourhoods."
whatElseYouSell.when: Build in the dry months, switch on after the next big storm.

whatElseYouSell.name: Jobsite signs for wall builds
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A wall going up on a hillside is visible from the whole street. A jobsite sign with your name and the site turns that into calls."

whatElseYouSell.name: Mailers to downhill neighbours
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Water problems run in streets. When you fix one yard, the houses on the same slope get a card showing the drainage fix."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, after each drainage job on a slope.

whatElseYouSell.name: Inspector and waterproofer referral sheet
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page sheet for home inspectors and basement waterproofers explaining which yard drainage problems you fix, with your contact."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the problem pages are live.

withoutAI.whoPays: The waterproofer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The waterproofer fixing the inside of the wall sends you the outside. I'll build their site and the two link to each other."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Inside and outside water fixes are sold to the same worried homeowner. The referral runs both ways.

withoutAI.route: Wall block and drainage supply yards
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your supply yard sells block, pipe and stone to every wall builder around and has a bare-bones site. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply yards have budgets and a contractor list that is your prospect list.

withoutAI.route: Civil engineers who stamp wall designs
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The engineer who stamps your taller walls gets residential calls with no way to take them. A simple request page fixes that."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small engineering firms rarely market themselves. The wall builder is a trusted, steady partner.

withoutAI.route: Gutter installers whose downspouts feed the yard
withoutAI.whoPays: The gutter company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Gutter crews see downspouts dumping against foundations every day. Their site can send the buried-line jobs to you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: The water problem starts at the roof and ends in the yard. Each trade feeds the other.

withoutAI.whoPays: The excavation contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The excavator you sub big digs to needs a site that shows grading and site prep. One introduction from you does it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Excavators rarely market and trust the wall builder who keeps them busy.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "HOAs with long entry and slope walls need a maintenance request page where residents report bulges and washouts."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Common-area walls are a liability worry, and the wall builder already inspects them.

withAI.route: Moisture complaint triage for the waterproofer
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners describe the wet wall and upload pictures, and the assistant sorts inside fixes from yard drainage, sending the yard jobs to your partner."
withAI.whyItWorks: It saves the waterproofer wasted visits and sends drainage work to the wall client.

withAI.route: Block and stone calculator for the supply yard
withAI.pitchLine: "Contractors enter wall length and height and get block, cap, geogrid and drainage stone quantities priced from that yard."
withAI.whyItWorks: It keeps wall builders ordering from one yard.

withAI.route: Residential enquiry screener for the engineer
withAI.pitchLine: "It asks homeowners the wall height, slope and soil questions the engineer needs, before anyone schedules a site visit."
withAI.whyItWorks: Engineers waste hours on calls that don't need them. The wall builder made the intro.

withAI.route: Wall inspection log for HOA managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents report wall bulges with a picture; the assistant logs location and severity and flags anything that needs the wall contractor this week."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards need a record of what they knew and when. The wall client gets the repair queue.

withAI.route: Downspout problem sorter for the gutter company
withAI.pitchLine: "Customers describe where the water goes after the downspout, and the assistant tells gutter and drainage jobs apart."
withAI.whyItWorks: Gutter crews already get these questions. Sorting them sends drainage work to your client.

withAI.route: Stormwater complaint intake for small towns
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents report flooding, washouts and blocked culverts with a picture and location; public works gets a sorted list."
withAI.whyItWorks: Small towns handle this by phone. The drainage client knows exactly what residents report.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for wet-yard calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Miss a call during a storm week and the caller gets a text asking for the address and a picture of where the water is sitting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and the wording approved.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for drainage and wall jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New reviews get a reply drafted that names the drain or wall and the storm it held through, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Drainage symptom checker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners answer where the water sits and when, and the checker points to the likely fix and a price range before you visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their fixes by symptom and typical price ranges.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and completion billing for wall jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit to book the dig, balance when the wall is capped or the drain is backfilled, each sent with a card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Picture triage for wall and water problems
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Uploaded pictures of a leaning wall or a soggy yard get sorted into urgent, site visit or simple fix, so storm weeks get handled in the right order."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a set of past job pictures labelled with what was done. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Storm-week dispatch board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After a storm, every drainage request sits on one board ranked by urgency, with addresses grouped so you see three wet yards on one street in one trip."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the request form live and their urgency rules.

softwareAI.name: After-hours water problem line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers at two in the morning, asks where the water is coming in, tells them what to do tonight from your notes, and books the drainage visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their calendar, overnight advice and screening questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Utility locate and wall permit reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a wall or drain job is booked, the locate request and the permit check get reminders on the right days, so the dig never waits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their booking flow and which towns require wall permits.

softwareAI.name: Wall material calculator for the crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter wall length, height and block type, and the foreman gets block, caps, geogrid layers, drainage stone and pipe in one list."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their block specs and geogrid rules by height.

softwareAI.name: Drainage chatbot on French drains and wall failure
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'is my wall leaning dangerously' and 'will a French drain fix this' from your own guidance, and books a visit when it can't tell."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their answers written once and current lead time. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with drainage plan and dig date
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner sees the drainage plan, the locate status and the dig date, and approves changes without a phone call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the dispatch board first.

softwareAI.name: Site-walk voice notes to scope
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the yard, describe the slope, the wet spot and the wall, and it drafts the scope and estimate with pipe lengths and stone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their estimate template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Drain flush and wall inspection reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each autumn, past drainage customers get a reminder to book a drain flush and a wall check before the wet season."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a list of past jobs and the inspection price.

softwareAI.name: Drainage plan sketcher from yard pictures
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From pictures and the address it drafts a rough plan of the yard's slope and a suggested drain route, for you to correct on the site visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a set of past drainage plans to tune against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Engineering package tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tracks each tall wall from survey to engineer's stamp to permit approval, so nobody digs before the drawings are back."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, for builders doing engineered walls. Needs their engineer's turnaround steps.

softwareAI.name: Project write-ups for drainage problem pages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From job notes and pictures it drafts a short problem-and-fix story for each drainage job, which you approve before it goes up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their notes and sign-off. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by wall type and drain length
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether boulder walls, block walls or French drains make the most once machine days, stone and dump fees are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs a season of receipts and crew days.

softwareAI.name: Crew app with geogrid and drainage stone checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The crew logs base depth, geogrid layers, pipe and drainage stone with a picture each course, so you can prove what's behind the wall."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, with two crews. Needs their build checklist and a foreman to pilot.

softwareAI.name: HOA and commercial wall bid sheet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Bids for common-area walls and drainage come together on one sheet with quantities, insurance and references."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, for contractors chasing HOA work. Needs two past bids.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for wall crew and operators
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for operator and wall crew roles say whether they've run a mini excavator and set block, and you only call the ones who have."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they hire. Needs must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Drainage symptom checker for every contractor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The symptom checker that sorts wet-yard calls for one drainage contractor works for every contractor fielding the same calls after a storm."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the logic; others load their own fixes and prices.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Certified wall builder locator for a block manufacturer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners who like your wall block need a certified builder. A locator with project galleries sends them to your trained crews."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund installer programs, and the wall client is the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your pipe, grates and emitters go into yards all over the region. A contractor finder sends homeowners to the crews who buy from you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want loyal contractors and lack a homeowner channel.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Landscape contractors' association wall and drainage kit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members get a symptom checker, a picture request form and wall engineering pages, ready to switch on."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need member benefits; one deal reaches many contractors.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with drainage clients rebuild the same problem pages each time. License the finished wall and drainage template."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the relationship; you supply the specialised build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Residents apply for the runoff cost-share program, upload the problem and get matched with approved drainage contractors."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Public programs run on paper and need cleaner applications. The drainage client knows the process.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The basement waterproofing franchise, per territory
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each waterproofing territory needs an exterior drainage page and request form that routes yard jobs to a partner. Built once, cloned per territory."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One agreement covers many territories, and every one has the same yard-water question.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New homes on sloped lots get drainage complaints after the first storm. A warranty request page routes them to one drainage contractor."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders want warranty calls handled cheaply. The drainage client becomes the default fixer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Property manager drainage and wall request portal
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every property you manage gets one page for flooding, washouts and leaning walls, with pictures and urgency."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Firms with many properties buy once; water damage is a constant worry.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Adjusters need a vetted list of wall and drainage contractors after storms. A referral page with documentation standards serves them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Adjusters value contractors who document well. The wall client is the first listing.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A drainage contractor in another metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "After every storm your phone fills with wet-yard calls you can't sort. I set up one drainage contractor per metro with this, and yours hasn't been claimed."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusive territory lets you reuse everything.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The contractor with a dead site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A drainage site that never got its request form working costs you every storm. I can move you onto a wall and drainage build that already takes requests for another contractor."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already chose to buy; they need someone who finishes.

upsellLadder.trigger: Rain in the forecast and a recently finished drain to film.
upsellLadder.line: "Rain's coming Thursday. Let's film your new drain working. That clip sells drainage better than any page."

upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of request forms show the same few symptoms over and over.
upsellLadder.line: "Most of your drainage requests describe the same three problems. The checker answers them with a range first."

upsellLadder.offer: Picture triage for wall and water problems

upsellLadder.line: "Last storm week you couldn't see everyone. Triage sorts the leaning walls from the puddles before you drive."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention double-trips across town or a second crew.
upsellLadder.line: "Two crews and storm weeks need one board for drainage jobs, grouped by street."

upsellLadder.offer: Drain flush and wall inspection reminders
upsellLadder.trigger: The wet season approaches with a full year of past drainage customers on file.
upsellLadder.line: "Everyone you fixed this year should get a drain flush before the wet season. That's a week of booked work."
